help.status.overview.title: Status and current channel
help.status.overview.body:
This page shows the channel Kodi is playing and the current automation state. The channel name comes from matching Kodi's TV channels to the M3U playlist. When Kodi supplies programme information, the programme title appears below it.

The state indicates whether detection is active, logo references are missing, detection has paused during the programme protection period, or playback is under manual control. Notices and errors appear below the three status cards. If Kodi cannot be reached, the page shows a connection message instead. Check the Kodi address and JSON-RPC web server under Kodi & Automation.
help.status.playback.title: On your screen
help.status.playback.body:
This card shows whether Kodi is playing the TV channel or the selected placeholder. During a change, it shows the switching state. The line below the placeholder says whether it was started automatically because the logo disappeared or started manually.

After an automatic switch, the monitor keeps watching the original channel. A manually started placeholder remains under your control until you return to the channel or resume automation.
help.status.duration.title: Duration
help.status.duration.body:
The timer counts the detected programme phase or advertising break since its last confirmed start. It does not know when a programme actually started before detection began. A manually started placeholder has no detected start either, so its display may stay at 0:00.

The programme protection period and placeholder minimum time are tracked separately. A notice shows their remaining time while either period is active.
help.status.detection.title: Logo detection
help.status.detection.body:
The monitor compares frames from the current channel with its saved logo references. “Logo found” means the channel logo was found in the checked frame; “Logo missing” can indicate an advertising break. An uncertain result does not trigger a switch.

A switch requires the configured number of consecutive clear frames and no active protection period. Without a reference, detection stays in setup mode. “Paused” means the detector was temporarily stopped during programme protection and will resume automatically afterwards.
help.status.controls.title: Control playback and automation
help.status.controls.body:
Start detection to begin monitoring the channel automatically; stop detection to end it. A temporary pause during the programme protection period still counts as enabled automation.

Play placeholder starts it manually. Play channel returns to the TV channel. Resume automation releases a manually started placeholder so automatic return can take over. End protection now ends only the current programme protection period and immediately restarts detection if that period paused it; the saved duration still applies after later advertising breaks.
help.status.diagnostic.title: Inspect logo detection
help.status.diagnostic.body:
The snapshot shows the most recently evaluated frame with its logo crop and mask. Similarity, edge and structure scores, contour coverage, position, and size help explain a match or uncertain result. Refresh snapshot loads a newer evaluation.

The two test-example buttons export the snapshot as a ZIP file. Label it according to whether the logo is actually visible, so the capture can be used as a correctly labeled test example. Exporting does not change live detection.
help.status.details.title: Technical details
help.status.details.body:
This section shows raw values for troubleshooting: matched channel, Kodi playback, placeholder source, detection mode, consecutive match and miss counters, similarity score, protection periods, and available references.

Connection, playback, and playlist errors appear with their technical messages. These values refresh regularly and are a snapshot, not a saved log file.
help.kodi.connection.title: Connect to Kodi
help.kodi.connection.body:
The JSON-RPC address connects the monitor to Kodi's web server, usually through the /jsonrpc path. The service uses it to read playback and channels and to control switching. Kodi's web server must be enabled and reachable from the device running this service.

Username and password are needed only if Kodi requires them for its web server. Save changes at the bottom of the page. Test Kodi connection checks reachability without changing playback.
help.kodi.channels.title: Channel playlist
help.kodi.channels.body:
Enter the URL of an M3U or M3U8 channel playlist. The monitor loads it at startup and refreshes it regularly. It provides the stream address used for logo detection.

The active Kodi TV channel is matched to a playlist entry by name. Kodi and M3U names therefore need an unambiguous match. Case, spaces, and punctuation are ignored. Without a matching entry, the monitor cannot reliably watch the channel.
help.kodi.network.title: Image address and network
help.kodi.network.body: The public base URL determines where Kodi can reach uploaded images, for example http://192.168.1.10:8099. Use this service’s network-accessible address. This setting is not required for Kodi file paths or external URLs.
help.placeholder.source.title: Random selection and date ranges
help.placeholder.source.body:
Enable the fillers you want to use. Each automatic or manual switch chooses one at random, which stays visible for the whole break. If at least two fillers are eligible, the last one shown is excluded.

Enabled seasonal fillers within their date ranges take priority over year-round fillers. Overlapping seasonal ranges share one selection pool. Annual ranges may span New Year, for example December 15 through January 6. February 29 only counts in leap years. One-time ranges include a year. Both boundary dates are included, using the server’s local time zone.

If no filler matches, the standard filler is used even when disabled or outside its date range. With neither a matching filler nor a standard, the channel keeps playing and an error appears. Removals and other changes take effect when saved. Removing the standard clears that selection. Fillers already playing remain available.
help.placeholder.image.title: Upload images
help.placeholder.image.body:
Select one or more JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP, or BMP files and click “Upload images”. Each image is added as an enabled filler. Existing images are kept. The first filler becomes the standard if none is selected. Each image can be up to 20 MB.

Uploading first saves your settings, then adds the images. Successful uploads are kept if a later image fails. Kodi must be able to reach the service’s public base URL. Check this address under “Kodi & automation” if Kodi runs on another device.
help.placeholder.files.title: Add Kodi files
help.placeholder.files.body:
Enter one path or URL per line that Kodi can open, such as a local image or video file or a Kodi-compatible network address. These paths are interpreted on the Kodi device.

“Add to list” adds entries to your selection without duplicating existing paths. Enable the fillers you want and optionally choose a date range. Click “Save” to apply these changes.
help.logos.editor.title: Select a channel image and logo
help.logos.editor.body:
Switch Kodi to the desired channel and use Load current image to capture a frame from its stream. Draw a tight rectangle around the logo that remains visible during the programme. The selection display shows its width and height.

Optimize selection trims the rectangle based on image detail if it includes too much surrounding picture. Save as reference creates a reference for the current channel. The first reference can start detection. Additional references with different backgrounds or logo variants improve reliability.
help.logos.mask.title: Image series and logo mask
help.logos.mask.body:
With a logo selected, capture a 30-second image series while the logo stays visible. Recurring contours form the suggested mask; changing parts of the image are treated as background. A useful series needs enough frames and varied backgrounds. If too few frames arrive, use a detection interval of three seconds or less.

Use Include area to mark contours that should be evaluated, or Exclude area to remove distracting background from the green mask. Brush radius sets the stroke size. The transparent preview shows the areas in use. Undo stroke and Restore automatic mask correct edits. Save mask and reference applies the changes or creates a new reference from the series.
help.logos.library.title: Saved references
help.logos.library.body:
This library shows comparison images only for the channel currently detected in Kodi. The monitor uses the best match among these references when checking its logo. Other channels have their own references.

Click an image to show its position and mask and edit them if needed. Delete removes only that reference. If you delete a channel's last reference, automatic logo detection for it cannot continue until a new reference is saved.
help.recognition.detection.title: Check interval and frame counts
help.recognition.detection.body:
The check interval sets the seconds between evaluated stream frames. A smaller number responds faster but performs more checks.

Logo missing sets how many clear consecutive frames without a logo are needed before switching automatically to the placeholder. Logo present sets the corresponding count for returning to the channel. Higher counts make detection steadier; lower counts shorten response time. Uncertain frames confirm neither presence nor absence and do not trigger a switch.
help.recognition.timing.title: Protection periods and pause
help.recognition.timing.body:
The programme protection period begins after an automatic return from the placeholder to the channel. During these seconds, another automatic switch to the placeholder is blocked. It does not begin at service startup or after a manual channel change. Set it to 0 to disable it. You can end an active period early from Status.

The placeholder minimum time begins with an automatically detected advertising break. Automation cannot return to the channel until it expires; fresh frames with a detected logo are then required. Setting it to 0 disables this hold.

Pause detection during programme protection also stops the detector and releases its stream connection for that period. Enabled detection resumes when the period ends. Manually stopped detection stays stopped.
help.recognition.advanced.title: Fine-tune logo detection
help.recognition.channels.title: Similarity threshold per channel
help.recognition.channels.body:
Set a separate similarity threshold for each channel here. A higher value requires a closer match to the saved logo; a lower value accepts larger differences. Values must be greater than 0 and at most 1. Adjust gradually and check the results with Inspect logo detection on the Status page.

A blank field uses the default similarity threshold from the advanced settings. The faint number in the field shows that default. Clear an existing value to use the default again. Refresh channel list reloads the playlist and keeps your edits. Save settings applies the changes.

The setting follows the channel's stream address. If that address changes in the playlist, the channel initially uses the default again.
help.recognition.advanced.body:
Under “Similarity threshold per channel”, you can set a value for each channel. A blank field always uses the current default similarity threshold from these advanced settings. Save the settings to apply changes. Values follow the stream URL; a changed URL initially uses the default again.

The similarity threshold from 0 to 1 determines how closely a checked image must match a reference. A higher value requires a closer match but may reject a real logo after it changes. Results near the threshold fall in an uncertainty band and do not trigger switching.

Contrast strength applies to older references without a saved mask. It emphasizes differences in the logo's brightness structure; current mask-based detection also considers contours and image structure. Adjust these values gradually and inspect real programme and advertising frames with Inspect logo detection on the Status page.
